newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on Tokyo sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on Tokyo sales.

text.p: Spot gold in Hong Kong ended slightly down on Tuesday from New York's previous close on slight selling from Japan, dealers said.
The metal was well supported by steady physical demand but activity was very quiet, they said.
Bullion ended at US$345.40/90 an ounce against New York's US$346.00/50 close on Monday.
"There is absolutely nothing going on and traders are getting tired of it," said one dealer at an international bank.
Traders reported light gold sales from Japan, but some said activity from the Tokyo Commodity Exchange had been subdued and sentiment remained bearish.
Dealers said buying was steady, particularly at $345 per ounce levels.
Gold was stuck in a tight range and dealers were waiting for prices to break above $350 per ounce or below $345 per ounce, gold sources said.
Local gold ended HK$8 lower at HK$3,200 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange dropped to -5.00 from its previous fix at +1.00
